The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=\pi.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $P(2,\pi,4)$ will be given by the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(2,\pi)}.$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂x}$ at $(2,\pi):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(2,\pi) & =(\pi)\cos((2)(\pi))+\cos(\pi) \\ & =(\pi)(1)+(-1) \\ & =-1 + \pi\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(2,\pi)} & =\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(2,\pi)}(x-(2)) \\ z-(4) & =(-1 + \pi)(x-(2)) \\ z & =- x + \pi x - 2 \pi + 6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(2,\pi,4)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes, as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=\pi \\ z=- x + \pi x - 2 \pi + 6\end{aligned}
$$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂x}$ at $(3,- \pi):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(3,- \pi) & =(- \pi)\cos((3)(- \pi))+\cos(- \pi) \\ & =(- \pi)(-1.0)+(-1.0) \\ & =-1.0 + 1.0 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(3,- \pi)} & =\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(3,- \pi)}(x-(3)) \\ z-(-1) & =(-1 + \pi)(x-(3)) \\ z & =- x + \pi x - 3 \pi + 2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(3,- \pi,-1)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes, as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=- \pi \\ z=- x + \pi x - 3 \pi + 2\end{aligned}
